finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches a caller-supplied URL. The only check is a suffix match, `host.endswith("example.com")`. That check does not require a dot boundary and is not strict set membership. Hosts such as `evilexample.com` or `example.com.attacker.net` do not pass, but `attackerexample.com` does. An attacker can register such a domain and point its DNS at 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1 or an RFC-1918 address. The server then requests that internal address. The response body is not returned, only `len(r.text)`, so this is semi-blind SSRF and the length leaks. Severity: MEDIUM. Redirect risk: no. httpx's default is follow_redirects=False, so redirects are not followed. The skill assumes httpx follows redirects by default; it does not, and that assumption was not applied here.
finding.source: `url` query parameter of GET /mirror (mirror.py:11), unauthenticated FastAPI route

trace.note: `url: str` is read from the query string and is attacker-controlled
`host.endswith("example.com")` is the only gate. It is a suffix check with no leading dot. `ALLOWED_SUFFIX = ".example.com"` at line 7 is defined but never used.
`c.get(url)` is called with the full original URL, including scheme, port and path

finding.guards_checked: The hostname suffix check at line 13 does not close the finding. The skill requires strict set membership, and the check is bypassable with a domain like `attackerexample.com`. The unused `.example.com` constant would have been a better check, but it is still a suffix check and would not close the finding either. There is no scheme or port restriction, no IP or CIDR block, no authentication on the route, and no DNS-rebinding protection. Redirects are not followed, because httpx defaults to follow_redirects=False. The response body is not returned, only its length, so this is MEDIUM rather than HIGH. The /ping route at line 23 uses a hardcoded URL and is not a finding.

verdict.guard_found: Only `host.endswith("example.com")` at mirror.py:13, a suffix check with no dot boundary. This does not close the finding. `ALLOWED_SUFFIX` at line 7 is unused. There is no scheme, port or IP restriction, and no auth.
verdict.reason: mirror.py:11 takes `url` from the query string, and the only gate at mirror.py:13 is a bypassable `endswith("example.com")` (e.g. attackerexample.com resolving to an internal IP). mirror.py:16 then fetches the full URL, so the semi-blind SSRF is real. Every trace line matches the description.
